venue.name: Tower Ranch Golf & Country Club (test)
venue.description: Tower Ranch is Kelowna's high-view public course: a Thomas McBroom design perched above the valley with sweeping views toward Okanagan Lake from nearly every hole, and a routing built around risk-reward decisions rather than length alone. It has been voted Best Course in Kelowna and ranked among Canada's top public courses by SCORE Golf, and Travel + Leisure named it one of the best new courses in the world when it opened. Worth knowing: there's no driving range on the property. Golfers loosen up on hitting nets, and Tower Ranch partners with World Beat Family Golf, just down the hill on Old Vernon Road, for full range sessions. The 10,000-square-foot clubhouse is a destination on its own, with Carrington's Restaurant & Patio sharing the same valley views, plus a fitness facility and event spaces. New for 2027: 9 & Dine, Monday to Wednesday after 4 PM, with a $30 food and drink voucher for Carrington's.
venue.address: 1855 Tower Ranch Blvd, Kelowna, BC V1P 1T9
venue.description_fr: Tower Ranch est le parcours public en altitude de Kelowna : un tracé de Thomas McBroom perché au-dessus de la vallée, avec une vue panoramique vers le lac Okanagan depuis presque chaque trou, et un parcours bâti autour de décisions risque-récompense plutôt que de la seule longueur. Il a été élu meilleur parcours de Kelowna et classé parmi les meilleurs parcours publics du Canada par SCORE Golf, et Travel + Leisure l'a nommé parmi les meilleurs nouveaux parcours au monde à son ouverture. Bon à savoir : il n'y a pas de champ de pratique sur place. Les golfeurs se réchauffent sur des filets d'exercice, et Tower Ranch s'est associé à World Beat Family Golf, un peu plus bas sur Old Vernon Road, pour les séances complètes au champ de pratique. Le pavillon de 10 000 pieds carrés est une destination en soi, avec le Carrington's Restaurant & Patio qui partage la même vue sur la vallée, ainsi qu'une salle d'entraînement et des espaces pour événements.

neighbours.name: Anytime Sim Golf
neighbours.description: Anytime Sim Golf is Kelowna's fully automated indoor golf simulator, built for golfers who'd rather skip the small talk and just play. Book a private bay online on Vaughan Avenue, and a secure CloudKey unlocks the door the moment you arrive: no front desk, no waiting. It runs day or night, 365 days a year, so a dawn session before work or a midnight round after a late shift both work fine. Bays use Foresight Sports launch monitors for real ball-flight data, and the contactless setup suits solo practice, quick lunch-break rounds, and small groups after a low-key, weather-proof way to play.

neighbours.name: Black Mountain Golf Club
neighbours.description: Black Mountain has earned its reputation as one of the Okanagan's most scenic public tracks: a par-71 layout that plays 6,400 yards across dramatic cliffside terrain, capped by a famous island-green par 3 that tests nerve as much as swing. Four sets of tees keep it approachable for high-handicappers while still rewarding accurate ball-striking from the tips, a big reason it has been named a PGA of BC Golf Facility of the Year and one of ScoreGolf's top-value public courses in Canada. PGA of Canada professionals are on hand for lessons if your swing needs a tune-up, and The Grill's patio, one of the nicest in the area, delivers valley views to match the round.
neighbours.address: 575 Black Mountain Dr, Kelowna, BC V1X 7K5

neighbours.name: Gallagher's Canyon Golf & Country Club — Canyon Course
neighbours.description: The Canyon Course is Gallagher's Canyon's championship stage: 18 holes, par 72, threading through ponderosa pine forest along the rim of a real canyon, with rock bluffs and forested drops framing shots on both nines. It's a physically dramatic round that rewards course management over brute length, minutes from downtown Kelowna and Okanagan Lake. Between rounds, the practice facility is one of the best in the valley: the Okanagan's only 300-plus-yard, double-ended grass driving range, two putting greens, two chipping greens with bunkers, and GBC Golf Academy instructors on hand for lessons. Semi-private membership keeps tee sheets civilized, and the Canyon Bar & Grill is the spot to unwind afterward. The 9-hole Pinnacle Course shares the same grounds and practice facilities.
neighbours.address: 4320 Gallagher's Drive West, Kelowna, BC V1W 3Z9

neighbours.name: Gallagher's Canyon Golf & Country Club — Pinnacle Course
neighbours.description: Pinnacle is Gallagher's Canyon's shorter, more relaxed sibling: a 9-hole, par-32 course sharing the same canyon-rim property as the championship Canyon Course, but built for a quicker, lower-pressure round. It's a good fit for beginners building confidence, families short on time, or low-handicappers wanting a fast tune-up before or after a full 18 elsewhere. Because it's part of the same semi-private facility, Pinnacle golfers get full run of the practice setup: the Okanagan's only 300-plus-yard double-ended grass driving range, two putting greens, two bunkered chipping greens, and GBC Golf Academy lessons. Finish with a meal at the Canyon Bar & Grill. If you want the full 18-hole championship test, the Canyon Course is right next door.
neighbours.address: 4320 Gallagher's Drive West, Kelowna, BC V1W 3Z9

neighbours.name: Golf Evolution
neighbours.description: Golf Evolution is where Kelowna golfers go to fix their swing, not just hit balls into a screen. Three GC Hawk simulator bays deliver tour-level club and ball data across 2,000-plus courses, and a UK PGA Professional runs lessons, club fitting and maintenance in the same Enterprise Way space. Credit-based Evo Packs (from $550 plus tax) last a year and can be shared with friends and family. Park around the building, take the elevator to level 2, and linger in the lounge over food and drinks.

neighbours.name: JSquared Golf
neighbours.description: JSquared Golf sits on the Gallagher's Canyon property but runs as its own indoor golf operation, built around instruction as much as simulator play. Its GCQUAD launch monitor uses four high-speed cameras to capture precise club and ball data, and PGA of Canada professionals John Mlikotic and Paul Wammer teach golfers of every level, from full swing fittings to ball-flight fixes. Open daily from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m., it's a serious practice option for Kelowna golfers who want real data behind every shot rather than a rough approximation. Being steps from the Gallagher's Canyon clubhouse means a session on the simulator can end with a meal or a drink at the Canyon Bar & Grill.

neighbours.name: Kelowna Driving Range & Mini Golf
neighbours.description: Kelowna's most complete practice facility and a fun night out: a 300-plus-yard grass range with 16 covered Toptracer stalls that track every shot. There's also a 4,700 sq ft bent-grass putting green, a short-game chipping area and an 18-hole championship mini-golf course for the whole family. Open daily to the public.

neighbours.name: Kelowna Golf & Country Club
neighbours.description: Kelowna Golf & Country Club is the Okanagan's only private golf and country club, and it plays like it: a classic 18-hole, par-72 parkland layout on Glenmore Drive, established in 1920 and shaped by architect A.V. Macan, refined over the decades while keeping its old-Kelowna character. Membership is limited and openings are rare, so this is a course built for people who golf often and want to know their course intimately, not book a tee time once a season. The practice facilities are a strength in their own right, with a practice range with TopTracer technology and a dedicated short-game area, and members also have a restaurant and PGA professionals for lessons.

neighbours.name: Kelowna Springs Golf Club
neighbours.description: Kelowna Springs is a course in transition, and worth playing for exactly that reason. The Les Furber layout that opened in 1990 was trimmed to its front nine for the 2025 season while the rest of the property was redeveloped, and the City of Kelowna has since reached a land-exchange agreement to bring the remaining holes into public hands, so this nine is here to stay. What's left is the best of it: spring-fed lakes that come into play again and again in north Kelowna near the airport, playable as a quick nine or as a full 18 by looping it twice. The clubhouse and warm-up areas stayed put through the change, and the same holes play differently the second time around.

neighbours.name: Michaelbrook Golf Course
neighbours.description: Michaelbrook is Kelowna's fast, easy round: a flat, walkable course that moves along at about three hours and ten minutes for 18 holes, so you can play without burning half a day. It's an approachable, forgiving layout that suits beginners, families, and anyone squeezing in a quick nine or eighteen after work, and since the City of Kelowna bought the property in 2025, with Monaghan Golf running it day to day, it remains an affordable tee time. The Brookside Grill's dog-friendly patio, just off the Rail Trail, is a good reason to stick around after your round; golfers and non-golfers alike drop by.

neighbours.name: Mission Creek Golf Club
neighbours.description: Mission Creek is a shorter, gentler round: 18 holes at a par of 61 across under 3,900 yards, winding through mature willows and cottonwoods and along ponds bordering the Mission Creek Greenway. It's been built and maintained by the same family for three generations, and it shows in how it's set up: forgiving for beginners and juniors but still useful for better players sharpening their irons and short game, with rounds typically wrapped inside three hours. There's a large putting green for warming up before you head out, and a golf instructor available if you want pointers. Grab something at the on-site restaurant afterward. It's less about length and more about a relaxed, scenic walk that doesn't eat your whole day.

neighbours.name: Okanagan Virtual Golf
neighbours.description: Okanagan Virtual Golf's Kelowna lounge, tucked into the Brewery District, treats indoor golf as a night out as much as a round of golf; its own tagline is "practice, party, play." Four bays run Uneekor EYE XO2 launch monitors on GSPro software, opening up roughly 2,000 virtual courses, from Okanagan favourites like Predator Ridge and Tower Ranch to Augusta and Pebble Beach. A fully licensed bar pours local craft beer, cocktails, and mocktails alongside big-screen seating, and the space keeps its social energy going with organized leagues. Come summer, it flips into an outdoor mini-putt pop-up, making it a year-round hangout as much as a simulator venue.

neighbours.name: Orchard Greens Golf Club
neighbours.description: Orchard Greens is one of the valley's more unusual short courses, laid out through a working Okanagan orchard so fairways and greens are carved between fruit trees rather than landscaping. It's a 9-hole, mid-length, par-32 track mixing par 3s, 4s and 5s, and the orchard changes with the season, so the course looks and plays differently depending on when you show up. Its signature move is stadium-lit night golf on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday evenings, no special gear required, just a different way to play once the sun goes down. It's a fun, low-pressure round for any level, well suited to couples or groups looking for something more memorable than a standard nine, with rentals available and Miss Pat's Kitchen on site for classic, stick-to-your-ribs food and a beer afterward.

neighbours.name: Shadow Ridge Golf Club
neighbours.description: Shadow Ridge is Kelowna golf without the fuss: a flat, walkable, par-71 course near the airport built for a relaxed, no-pretense round rather than a test of championship nerves. It plays fast and the rates are easy on the wallet, which makes it a solid pick for casual golfers, first-timers, or anyone squeezing in a round on a budget. There's a putting practice area to loosen up before you tee off, a well-stocked golf shop with club and cart rentals, and a full-service restaurant that welcomes non-golfers and draws a local crowd on its own. If you want a laid-back track that doesn't take itself too seriously, this is it.

neighbours.name: Simplex Sportszone
neighbours.description: Simplex Sportszone is an indoor sports arcade that takes golf seriously: Trackman 4 and Full Swing studios offer 400-plus courses, with in-house PGA coaches on hand. The 6,000-square-foot licensed building adds hockey, baseball, soccer and other simulators plus six full-motion racing cockpits (ages 14 and up). Studios hold up to four players, from about $36.75 an hour Monday to Thursday; bring clubs or rent for $10, and plan an hour per golfer for 18 holes. Booking ahead is wise, and groups up to 40 can party here.

neighbours.name: Sunset Ranch Golf & Country Club
neighbours.description: Scotty Creek winds through 10 of the 18 holes at Sunset Ranch, a semi-private, par-72 course on rolling Kelowna terrain minutes from the airport. Mature trees frame tight, strategic fairways across about 6,500 yards, and Golf Digest listed it among its Best Places to Play in 2009. There's no driving range, only hitting nets, so warm up on the putting and chipping greens; the Golf Academy offers lessons. The clubhouse has a 120-seat dining room, a 40-seat lounge and two patios.
neighbours.address: 5101 Upper Booth Rd S, Kelowna, BC V1X 7V8

neighbours.name: The Fringe Indoor Golf
neighbours.description: The Fringe Indoor Golf is Kelowna's 24/7, staffless simulator space in the AQUA building right off Lakeshore. Book online, and secure mobile access with emailed entry details replaces a front desk. Four Trackman iO bays (three open, one private room) track every shot across more than 300 virtual courses, with Trackman tournaments for anyone chasing bragging rights. A quiet, naturally lit lounge feels more private club than warehouse, and hourly rates of about $40 to $80, with member discounts, suit beginners and low-handicappers alike.

neighbours.name: The Okanagan Golf Club — Bear Course
neighbours.description: The Bear is Jack Nicklaus's take on Okanagan golf: a par-72 course stretching to 6,852 yards through ponderosa pine forest, with wider, more receptive fairways than its sister course next door. It's the longer of The Okanagan Golf Club's two 18s but the more forgiving one, favouring golfers who want to make a decisive strike from the tee without punishing every miss. As part of this 36-hole, semi-private GolfBC facility, Bear golfers get a strong practice setup: a double-ended grass driving range plus dedicated chipping and putting areas, with GBC Golf Academy instructors available. The Spanish Southwest-style clubhouse houses the golf shop and Table Nineteen restaurant, a solid stop for a post-round meal on the patio. The Quail Course, sharing the property, is the tighter, more demanding option.

neighbours.name: The Okanagan Golf Club — Quail Course
neighbours.description: The Quail is the more demanding of The Okanagan Golf Club's two courses: a Les Furber design from 1994 that's shorter than its sister Bear Course at 6,576 yards and par 71, but tighter and more strategic, winding through ponderosa pines across the more mountainous, elevation-changed part of the property. You won't always reach for the driver here; positioning matters more than power. It's part of the same 36-hole, semi-private GolfBC facility as the Bear, so Quail golfers share the double-ended grass driving range and dedicated chipping and putting greens, plus GBC Golf Academy lessons if you want them. The Spanish Southwest-style clubhouse's Table Nineteen restaurant and patio are a good finish to the round. If you want a longer, more open test, the Bear is right there.

neighbours.name: Ailm Estate
neighbours.description: The newest chapter from one of the Okanagan's founding wine families, Ailm Estate pours its sparkling Reserve Brut and estate wines on a covered patio above the orchards of southeast Kelowna. It still feels like a discovery: small, unhurried and personal, the kind of tasting you'll be telling friends about before everyone else finds it. Open Thursday to Sunday.

neighbours.name: Ancient Hill Winery
neighbours.description: Ancient Hill Winery brings a European sensibility that's rare among Kelowna wineries: boutique in scale and unhurried in pace, with no pressure to rush through a tasting. The outdoor seating is built for picnics, so bring your own spread, find a shaded table and let the visit turn into the whole afternoon.

neighbours.name: Azhadi Vineyards
neighbours.description: Azhadi Vineyards is a striking Persian-inspired winery in Kelowna whose architecture is based on Tehran's Azadi Tower, with handmade Persian rugs and art inside. Book the curated wine-and-food pairing, served with sweeping valley views.

neighbours.name: Antico Pizza Napoletana
neighbours.description: Antico Pizza Napoletana bakes its pies in a wood-fired oven built in Naples, where a ninety-second bake gives the crust its charred, soft and chewy edge. The dough rises for a day or more, the tomatoes are San Marzano, and the pizzeria is recognized by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana. Ordering is at the counter on Bernard Avenue, with no reservations needed, and staff are patient with families and picky young eaters.

neighbours.name: Aomi Sushi Japanese Restaurant
neighbours.description: Yakiudon and sashimi have long been the reasons to visit Aomi Sushi, a small, low-key Japanese restaurant on Lakeshore Road that longtime Lower Mission diners still count among their favourites. The menu sticks to dependable standards rather than flashy specials. First-timers do well to start with those two and branch out from there.

neighbours.name: Apni Rasoi Taste of India
neighbours.description: The samosas at Apni Rasoi come out flaky and genuinely fresh, not the frozen, reheated version too common at quick Indian takeout spots. This Rutland kitchen has built its reputation on portions that feel generous relative to the price, the kind of value that makes you order more than you planned. It's takeout-focused and unpretentious, no dining room theatrics, just a kitchen that consistently gets the basics right. At 4.2 stars, it's a dependable go-to rather than a destination, which is exactly the role a great neighbourhood takeout spot should play. Grab a few samosas as a starter no matter what else you order. Simple, reliable, and worth the stop.
neighbours.address: 538 Hollywood Rd S, Kelowna, BC V1X 3T3
